verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਜਾਣੀਐ ਸਚੇ ਸਚਾ ਨਾਉ ਧਰਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: gur paramesar jaaneeaai sache sachaa naau dharaiaa|

en.bdb: The Guru ought to be known as the Supreme Lord because only that true being has adopted the true name (of the Lord).

verses.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰੁ ਆਕਾਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਏਕੰਕਾਰ ਅਪਾਰੁ ਸਦਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: nira(n)kaar aakaar hoi eka(n)kaar apaar sadhaiaa|

en.bdb: The formless Lord has made His self known in the form of Ekaiikar, the one boundless Being.

verses.gurmukhi: ਏਕੰਕਾਰਹੁ ਸਬਦ ਧੁਨਿ ਓਅੰਕਾਰਿ ਅਕਾਰੁ ਬਣਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: eka(n)kaarahu sabadh dhun oa(n)kaar akaar banaiaa|

en.bdb: From Ekanka came up Oankar, the Word vibration which further came to be known as the world, full of names and forms.

verses.gurmukhi: ਇਕਦੂ ਹੋਏ ਤਿਨ ਦੇਵ ਤਿਹੁਂ ਮਿਲਿ ਦਸ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਗਣਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: eikadhoo hoe tin dhev tihu(n) mil dhas avataar ganaiaa|

en.bdb: From the one Lord came out three gods (Brahma-, Visnu and Mahes'a) who further got themselves counted among the ten incarnations (of the supreme Being).

verses.gurmukhi: ਆਦਿ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਆਦੇਸੁ ਹੈ ਓਹੁ ਵੇਖੈ ਓਨ੍ਹਾ ਨਦਰਿ ਨ ਆਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: aadh purakh aadhes hai oh vekhai onhaa nadhar na aaiaa|

en.bdb: I salute this primal Being who sees them all but is Himself invisible.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸੇਖ ਨਾਗੁ ਸਿਮਰਣੁ ਕਰੈ ਨਾਵਾਂ ਅੰਤੁ ਬਿਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: sekh naag simaran karai naavaa(n) a(n)t bia(n)t na paiaa|

en.bdb: The mythical snake (Sesanag) recites and remembers Him through His myriad names but even then knows nothing about His ultimate extent.
The true name of same Lord is loved by gurmukhs.
